messages:
security-bot: [ALERT] Cloud asset scanner detected an overly permissive IAM binding: `roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter` granted to serviceAccount:analytics-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com AND a publicly readable S3 bucket `redwood-prod-archive-logs` with recent objects (s3://redwood-prod-archive-logs/2026-03-20/). -- Evidence: https://console.cloud.google.com/asset-inventory?alert=1825001234 :eyes:

emma: tagging: @oncall-sre @raj — is this real data exposure or a false positive?

raj: quick look: Bucket has ACL `public-read` on prefix `2026-03-20/` per the scanner. KMS key IAM shows the SA in both project and key policy. Might be accidental binding from deployment job last week.

oncall-sre: on it. First step: remove public access to the S3 objects and revoke SA key permissions. Will run containment now.

oncall-sre: running: `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-prod-archive-logs --acl private`
noncall-sre: running: `aws s3 rm s3://redwood-prod-archive-logs/2026-03-20/ --recursive --profile prod` (will snapshot to secure archive first)

lisa: please snapshot before deletion. we need audit for legal. Create a temp export to secure, access-controlled bucket: `s3://redwood-incident-archive/1825001234/` and restrict to security only.

oncall-sre: doing snapshot -> `aws s3 sync s3://redwood-prod-archive-logs/2026-03-20/ s3://redwood-incident-archive/1825001234/ --acl bucket-owner-full-control`

dylan: i'll rotate the KMS key policy and remove that SA from key permissions. Also recommend rotating any long-lived credentials used by the analytics runner.

dylan: steps I'm taking now:
```
# remove SA from key IAM
gcloud kms keys remove-iam-policy-binding data-key \ 
  --location global --keyring rrx \ 
  --member serviceAccount:analytics-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \ 
  --role roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter --project redwood-prod

# confirm
gcloud kms keys get-iam-policy data-key --keyring rrx --location global --project redwood-prod
```

emma: also log and preserve Cloud Audit Logs for KMS and S3 for the last 30 days. we need to know what that SA accessed.

security-bot: Saved logs link: https://logging.redwood.example.com/archives/1825001234. KMS Decrypt events: 2026-03-20T09:42:11Z by analytics-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com (request-id: a1b2c3). S3 GET on public object: 2026-03-20T09:43:05Z from IP 34.120.11.8.

raj: looks like data exfiltration window ~ 09:42–09:46 UTC. We should rotate any credentials accessible to that SA and revoke tokens.

lisa: I'll open an incident ticket in PagerDuty and assign to sec-ops. Also cc legal and customer-success for any customer-facing impact.

oncall-sre: ACL set to private, objects synced to incident archive, original objects removed from public prefix. Confirmed no 200 responses on public path now.

dylan: KMS SA removed from key policy. For defense-in-depth, I'll add a deny policy on the key binding to block principals outside of `redwood-prod` service accounts. Drafting PR to terraform: `modules/kms/deny_external_sa.tf`

emma: Good. Post-incident actions: 1) Add automated rule to detect `public-read` on prod buckets and auto-block, 2) Enforce least-privileged role on CI service accounts (no broad KMS roles), 3) Add terraform plan gate in CI that flags IAM changes involving `roles/cloudkms.*` or `roles/owner`.

security-bot: created incident record INC-2026-042. Checklist added: containment, evidence preservation, customer notification draft, IAM remediation PR link.

raj: one more: run `gcloud iam service-accounts keys list --iam-account=analytics-runner@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and revoke any user-managed keys.

oncall-sre: revoked all user-managed keys for that SA and rotated the CI token used by analytics pipeline. Pushed emergency terraform change to remove public ACLs and lock bucket policies (PR: #4123).

lisa: we'll do a postmortem in 48 hours. Owner: emma. Action items assigned in the ticket. Recommend communication template: short notice to affected internal teams, longer draft for customers if we confirm customer data exposure.

emma: thanks everyone. please add any follow-ups to INC-2026-042 and ensure audit logs preservation retention is extended for this incident. :white_check_mark:
